source.title: Topographic Training Concentrates Causal Circuits Without Improving Neuron Monosemanticity
source.authors: Gautam Ranka; S. Pandere; Aiden Dsouza

record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron-level selectivity under a training-time regularizer, a different measurement from the claim’s audit of neuron-pole jobs. It tests whether this regularization changes monosemanticity, but does not test the stated audit shares.
record.gate_note: The study reports additional results on SAE feature sparsity, spatial coherence, and causal patching. These do not directly measure the specific claim-version quantities of interpretable-neuron shares or attribution-graph reconstruction; related findings are recorded as none where they bear on the claim's subject. Accuracy values are used as a capability check, not as claim rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It adds a training-time spatial regularizer (TopoLoss) to ViT-S and TinyViT on ImageNet-100. It then measures entropy-based class selectivity (Mu), SAE L0 and dead features, and patching ratios. V4 says messy neurons come from architecture, regularization choices and weak tools, and that the interpretable-neuron share rises with better tools and modern architectures. Testing whether one added regularizer raises class selectivity is a different question. Mu is also not an interpretable-neuron share: a neuron with low class entropy-selectivity can still have one coherent job that cuts across classes, and the authors themselves flag the class-basis limitation. The study does not cite or discuss the essay or the automated-explanation work. Its results are related findings, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that neuron-level monosemanticity metrics may be insensitive to circuit-level interpretability gains, and that cheap architectural priors can complement post-hoc tools. In TinyViT, they report the H2 trend replicates but H3 does not transfer.
record.recipe_differences: The cited audit concerns neuron-pole job explanations; this study trains vision transformers with a spatial weight-smoothness penalty and measures entropy-based class selectivity, SAE feature statistics, and activation-patching ratios.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects vary with TopoLoss alpha. In TinyViT, causal patching ratios peak at alpha=0.1 rather than alpha=1.0; the TinyViT results use a single seed.

fits_no_version.finding: In ViT-S, TopoLoss leaves neuron-level entropy class-selectivity flat across alpha (0.234 to 0.236, n.s.). SAE-feature Mu is also flat (0.021 to 0.026). TinyViT Mu is 0.249 to 0.262, from a single seed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Laplacian weight-smoothness training penalty does not change per-neuron class selectivity in small vision transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: At alpha=1.0, SAE L0 falls 11% and the dead-feature fraction rises from 0.2% to 3.8%. Accuracy partly confounds this (R2=0.72). Alpha=0.1 shows no reliable effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Strong topographic regularization reduces SAE-measured feature complexity, partly via accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-activated 16-unit clusters have higher patching ratios than random sets, rising with alpha (1.68, 2.27, 2.79). The effect is weak in TinyViT (at most 1.42x).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topographic training concentrates causal patching mass into spatially local neuron clusters.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, Seoul, South Korea, 2026
record.problems: The study uses only ImageNet-100; the ViT-S SAE L0 result has an unresolved accuracy confound; TinyViT results are single-seed and differ from ViT-S in several factors; the neuron-selectivity measure uses ImageNet classes as its concept basis, which the authors note may miss features crossing class boundaries.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out for the 60-row limit. Other reported results, including spatial coherence and SAE-feature Mu at 25k images, were not extracted as rows because they do not directly measure the version-specific quantities; the paper's summary and discussion report that SAE-feature Mu is also flat.

untested.parts: No comparison of interpretability tools or architectures, no interpretable-neuron share, and no InceptionV1-sized estimates. The study only tests whether an added spatial regularizer changes class-entropy selectivity.
No language models and no scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 neurons and no polysemantic-example analysis.
No attribution graphs and no replacement-model comparison.
No test of explanations from activating examples against held-out activations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'challenges' label is removed. An added regularizer that fails to raise class-entropy selectivity does not contradict V4, which attributes messiness to architecture, regularization choices and tools, and predicts gains from better tools and architectures. Mu is also not a share of interpretable neurons. The paper assumes the superposition framing and never engages the essay's claims.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimate the shares with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood poles.
Tests neither language models nor dense-versus-MoE comparisons or scaling to large parameter counts.
Does not study the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, or recursive generalization.

Tests TopoLoss in ViT-S and a preliminary TinyViT probe using entropy-based class selectivity, not the claimed percentage of interpretable neurons. It does not compare interpretability tools or test the essay's InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Uses activation patching on neuron clusters, but does not test attribution graphs, behavioral reconstruction, or replacement-model error.
Does not test explanations built from activating examples against held-out activation predictions.
Does not evaluate automated neuron-explanation scores on new text.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean neuron class-selectivity using normalized negative entropy (Mu).
rows.uncertainty: ± values reported; no statistically significant alpha-level comparison
rows.note: The authors report that neuron-level Mu is flat across alpha and that no alpha-level comparison is statistically significant.
rows.check: Class-selectivity entropy under an added regularizer is not V4's interpretable-neuron share, and TopoLoss is not the architecture or tool improvement V4 names. Relinked to none; the state (flat Mu, n.s.) is correct.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean neuron class-selectivity using normalized negative entropy (Mu).
rows.uncertainty: ± values reported; comparison described as not significant
rows.note: The authors conclude that TopoLoss does not change neuron-level class selectivity.
rows.check: Same as r1: the construct differs from V4. Values 0.2359 vs 0.2340, n.s., match Table 4.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured fraction of neurons with Mu greater than 0.5.
rows.note: No uncertainty or statistical comparison is reported for this fraction; the authors state that no alpha-level neuron-Mu comparison is statistically significant.
rows.check: Fraction with Mu>0.5 rises from 0.26% to 0.52%, with no uncertainty reported. It is not V4's measure; relinked to none.

rows.operation_detail: Measured fraction of neurons with Mu greater than 0.5.

rows.check: Fraction with Mu>0.5 rises from 0.26% to 0.78%, with no uncertainty reported. Not V4's measure; relinked to none.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE mean active features per token (L0) at layer 6.
rows.uncertainty: p = 0.054 for the alpha=0.1 L0 effect; uncertainty for this value not stated in Appendix Table 6
rows.note: The authors say the alpha=0.1 L0 effect is not reliable. This is a feature-complexity proxy, not an audit of canonical polysemantic neurons.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured SAE mean active features per token (L0) at layer 6.
rows.note: The paper calls this suggestive but notes an accuracy confound: validation accuracy falls from 61.2% to 59.6%, and the accuracy-L0 regression has R2 = 0.72, p = 0.004.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Measured fraction of dead SAE features at layer 6.
rows.note: This is an SAE feature-complexity result, not a count of neuron poles with one or more jobs.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Patched the top-k=16 class-activated neuron cluster from a target-class image into an other-class image and compared its absolute logit delta with a random size-16 set.
rows.baseline: Random unit sets of the same size; ratio reference = 1
rows.note: The study reports this as the unregularized comparison condition; it does not test attribution-graph reconstruction.
rows.check: This is the alpha=0 reference condition for the H3 comparison, not an effect row in itself.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16
rows.operation_detail: Patched the top-k=16 class-activated neuron cluster from a target-class image into an other-class image and compared its absolute logit delta with a random size-16 set.
rows.baseline: Random unit sets of the same size; ratio reference = 1
rows.note: This measures relative causal patching sufficiency, not whether an attribution graph reconstructs model behavior.

rows.subject: ViT-S/16

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: ViT-S/16 with TopoLoss alpha=0.1 and alpha=1.0, three seeds
reader_labels.reason: The measured neuron-level selectivity scores are flat across alpha, and the authors report no statistically significant alpha-level comparisons (r1-r2). This tests only the TopoLoss/entropy-selectivity part of V4, not its estimates of interpretable-neuron shares.
